audit.whatIsWrong: Three of Aurora's five abilities were given invented names, the fourth was described backwards, and the passive was described as the wrong kind of ability entirely. 'Twin Slicebeam' (Q), 'Twofold Movement' (W) and 'The Weight of Worlds' (R) do not exist. The full layer names Twofold Hex but calls it her escape/blink — Twofold Hex is the Q missile; the blink is Across the Veil (W). And spikes[2] and the late block credit her passive with 'true damage': Spirit Abjuration heals her, it does no damage at all.
audit.why: Riot's kit lists Spirit Abjuration (P), Twofold Hex (Q, 900, 9s), Across the Veil (W, 700, 22/21/20/19/18s), The Weirding (E, 825, 15s), Between Worlds (R, 140/120/100s). The packet's own defects field already records that this matchup 'never names any of Aurora's abilities'.
audit.corrected: Real names throughout; the focus target moved from Twofold Hex to Across the Veil, which is the escape the whole page was trying to describe; the passive corrected from true damage to healing, which also makes Grievous Wounds the right answer to it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Between Worlds is described as displacing you off your tentacles, in five places.
audit.why: Riot's text: she leaps, releases a shockwave that damages and slows, then creates an area that slows enemies inside it and lets Aurora teleport from one side of it to the other. It slows you and repositions her; it does not move you. A player who plans around being displaced will position wrongly.
audit.corrected: Level 6 rewritten as a slow zone she teleports across, on a 140s cooldown at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 3 is set to Aurora in both layers while its own why says 'W Harsh Lesson lets you occasionally catch her for an even level 3'.
audit.why: The packet levelChart has Skill at row 2 and the mirror audit (aurora__illaoi) also set row 2 to Skill. Both layers and both directions agree once this one row moves.
audit.corrected: phases[2].side and win[2] set to Skill as a paired group.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never states what her blink actually costs her against your E.
audit.why: Riot's text for Test of Spirit: the target becomes a Vessel if it gets too far from the spirit. Across the Veil is a 700-range leap on a 22s cooldown — blinking away from her own spirit is what turns her into a tentacle farm, which is the single answer Illaoi has to a champion with two escapes.
audit.corrected: Stated in spikes[0] and report[5]: bait the blink, then land E — and if she blinks off the spirit, she Vessels herself.

audit.whatIsWrong: Aurora is 'he'/'him' in tradeGood, the trading and wave breakdowns, the report and the feeding block.
audit.why: Template text stamped in without a gender pass.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed in place, same length.

notes: The _missing entry for this matchup says 'Your Leap of Faith (R) shuts off Aurora's Across the Veil (W), Between Worlds (R)'. That is derived from the 'grounding' flag on Illaoi's R, and Riot's own description of Leap of Faith says only that it damages nearby enemies and spawns a tentacle per champion hit. Per the description-beats-flag rule I did not write it; the mirror audit (aurora__illaoi) removed the matching untargetability claim for the same reason. Left for the user: the mirror set row 6 (2+ items) to Illaoi, while this page and the packet both have Aurora, and every piece of prose on both layers describes a full-item Aurora kiting you. I did not flip that row because I cannot verify a late-game power shift toward Illaoi and inventing one is worse than leaving the mirror to reconcile it.
